name: Traffic Grey A
lede: Traffic Grey A is a bluish grey from the German RAL road-and-signage standard, one of a matched pair with Traffic Grey B.

sections.title: One of a RAL pair
sections.body:
RAL, founded in 1927, lists this hue as RAL 7042, and the hex value here is a screen approximation of that spec [1]. It is paired in the standard with the darker [[traffic-grey-b]], the two meant to read together on road markings and signage [1]. The books give no account of why RAL split its traffic greys into an A and a B rather than naming them separately, so that choice is undocumented [1].

The nearest named neighbor in our library is [[hathi-grey]], close enough that the two are easy to confuse on screen [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds this hue, as photographed, in 526 of 23,781 paintings (2.21 percent), more common than 75 percent of the named colors we track [2]. It peaks in the 1600s, in 88 of 6,394 paintings, at 1.2 times the expected rate for the 6,394 paintings we have from that century [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays a light, in 51 percent of its 272 occurrences [2].

[[painter:bernardo-bellotto|Bernardo Bellotto]] is its most devoted painter here, carrying it in 5 of 20 of his works, 7.2 times his home museums' baseline [2]. The earliest matching painting is dated 1360, 567 years before RAL recorded the standard in 1927, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. It shares canvases more than chance with [[nickel]] and [[french-grey]] [2].
